Where it began

Babar Azam's family comes from the Walled City of Lahore, and he was born on 15 October 1994. Cricket was close to home: his older cousins Kamran and Umar Akmal both played for Pakistan, and their stories persuaded him that the game could be a life.

Before he played at Gaddafi Stadium, he worked there as a ball boy. His first coach, Rana Sadiq, gave him the basics of batting, and from there he made his way into Pakistan's under-19 side.

The player

Babar's Test debut came against the West Indies in Dubai in October 2016, and he made 69 in his first innings. By October 2026 he had played 66 Tests, scoring 4,771 runs at 42.98 with nine hundreds and 34 fifties.

Some of those innings carry a particular warmth. When Test cricket came home to Pakistan in December 2019 after ten years away, he made an unbeaten hundred at Rawalpindi in his first Test innings on home soil. In Karachi in 2022 he faced 425 balls and made 196 against Australia, the best fourth-innings score any Test captain has made. He has led Pakistan in 24 Tests, winning 11, and in July 2026 he was asked to lead them again.

What made him special

His batting is built on balance and timing rather than force. He plays late, picks gaps, keeps the scoreboard turning and punishes anything loose, and his cover drive is the shot everyone waits for. He has been just as good in the shorter formats, ranked the best ODI batsman in the world and, by 2025, the leading run-scorer in T20 internationals.

His bowling has been rather less in demand. He has two Test wickets at 21.00, with a best of one for one. On those figures, captains may have been a little hasty in keeping the ball away from him.

Away from the middle

Babar has been honoured at home and abroad. He was the ICC's Cricketer of the Year for 2022, and the following year, at 28, he became the youngest cricketer to receive the Sitara-i-Imtiaz, one of Pakistan's highest civilian awards. He is known, fondly, as King Babar.

He has played league cricket all over the world, Somerset among his clubs, and in 2026 he led Peshawar Zalmi to the Pakistan Super League title, his first as captain.

And finally

It is a long walk from the boundary rope at Gaddafi Stadium to the middle. Babar made it first as a boy fetching the ball back, and then as the man who keeps sending it there.
